title: Trip recap with Sam
description: Demo conversation (synthetic, for the demo account). Back from the coast trip, Alex and Sam relive the lighthouse town, the motel night and a raccoon at the campground, Sam finally tells the story of the cousin's wedding, and they return to the lighthouse.

utterances.text: Okay, I finally sorted the photos. Four hundred and twelve. Most of them are the lighthouse.
As they should be. That town was my favorite part of the whole trip.
Same. The fog rolling in at five, and the foghorn going every thirty seconds.
And we climbed the lighthouse right before it closed. A hundred and twenty steps.
A hundred and twenty-two. You skipped two.
I was saving my legs for the half marathon. Okay, but the motel. Night three.
The motel was a choice.
It had a shower that wasn't a coin box. That was my only requirement.
It also had a painting of a horse staring directly at my bed.
Ha. You turned it to the wall at two in the morning.
I couldn't sleep with it judging me. But the best night was the campground after.
The raccoon night.
The raccoon night. We left the cooler by the tent and woke up to this tiny bandit eating our tortillas.
And you yelled, those are for tacos, like he'd understand.
He took the whole bag. Looked me in the eye and walked off.
At least Theo's tent survived the rain. I promised to bring it back dry.
Barely dry. Okay, can I finally tell you about my cousin's wedding? I keep promising.
Yes! You've been teasing this since before the trip.
So, outdoor wedding on a farm. Beautiful. Then halfway through the vows, a goat gets loose and walks right down the aisle.
No.
And it eats half the bouquet. The flower girl starts crying, the goat won't budge, and my uncle tries to carry it out like a sack of potatoes.
Please tell me the rings were okay.
The rings were fine. But the goat is in half the photos. They put it on the thank-you cards.
That's the best wedding I've ever heard of.
My cousin says it's the only reason anyone remembers the vows. Anyway, that's the chaos.
Totally worth the wait. But back to the lighthouse. Did you get the one of the beam at night?
I did, from the beach. The light sweeping over the water.
Send it to me. I want to print it.
It's already in the album. Same town next summer?
Same town. Different motel. No horse.
